steps.name: frame the question
steps.instructions: Frame the spike: restate the question in one sentence, the decision it should make possible, and what data would settle it (numbers, limits, versions, compatibility, cost, effort). Name what the question needs from outside this repository (third-party APIs, libraries, SDKs, webhooks, vendor docs: exact field names, formats, versions, limits), or say it needs nothing from outside. Then list two to four distinct angles to research (options, approaches or tools), each one researchable on its own. Do not research them yet. If the decision depends on something only the person knows, ask it once: at most 3 questions, each with 2 to 4 options (the recommended one first), in one ```keel-questions block after the angles (a JSON list of {"id", "question", "why", "options": [{"label", "description", "recommended"}]}). Ask only about the DECISION the spike must support: do we need it at all, for whom, what certainty or what evidence decides it, deadline or cost limits, which options to compare. Never ask how to build it (which column or table, overwrite or keep history, which systems or APIs read it, a field's format): those belong in the feature's spec interview, so list them under "Open questions for the spec" in your framing, and the findings carry them on. When the answers come back, frame the spike again with them.

steps.name: research the outside docs
steps.instructions:
Research what this spike needs from outside the repository: the third-party APIs, libraries, SDKs, webhooks and their docs that the question and its angles depend on (field names, payload formats, versions, limits). Search first, then fetch the best sources; never conclude from one failed URL. Edit nothing. If the question needs nothing from outside the repository, say so in one line and end with CONFIDENCE: high. The framing, with its question and angles:
{{data.frame_text}}

steps.name: one researcher per angle
findings + recommendation
start a feature flow from the findings
